statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. headline: NQ holds 29,597.00 in a two-sided 136-point Globex range with tail at 7, while Brent at $99.51 and a 4.806% 10-year lift stress to 75
body: As of the assessment cutoff the Nasdaq-100 shows no mean-reversion failure. NQ futures trade at 29,597.00, up 58.25 points or about 0.20%, inside a Globex range of 29,489.75-29,625.50. That range is 135.75 points, roughly 0.46% wide, and it is two-sided with no gap from the 29,538.75 settle. The overnight high has been extended only marginally over the past hour and price sits below it, so retracement quality is intact and no shallow-pullback or failed-retracement pattern is present. E-mini S&P 500 futures at 7,684.50 are up just 0.05% inside a 15-point range, a clear cross-index conflict with any directional reading of NQ. Tuesday's cash session was split rather than trending: the Nasdaq-100 closed at 29,507.70, down 0.12% within a 29,400.70-29,655.73 range, the S&P 500 fell 0.58% to 7,673.52 and the Nasdaq Composite fell 0.32% to 26,421.41, while the Dow dropped 628.18 points or 1.18% to 52,786.07. Internals stayed sharply dispersed, with Intel, AMD, Arm, Qualcomm, Broadcom and Tesla higher against declines in Nvidia, Apple, Microsoft and Micron. That dispersion supports a mixed dominant mode rather than trend structure. The stress backdrop remains materially heavier than the price path. Brent trades at $99.51, up 1.62% in a fourth consecutive higher session and at a near seven-week high, with WTI around $94.4. The driver is the ongoing tanker conflict in and around the Strait of Hormuz, where U.S. forces disabled or destroyed three Iranian crude carriers including one off Kharg Island after ballistic missiles were fired toward a U.S. carrier and a destroyer, alongside Houthi strikes on Saudi energy infrastructure including the Jazan refinery. Reporting on 8 September added a previously undisclosed second wave of Iranian attacks on U.S. Navy vessels on Monday in which no American ship was hit, and Iran separately claimed a strike on a U.S. vessel that the U.S. military denied. Hormuz throughput remains far below pre-conflict levels, leaving a large unresolved supply-risk premium. The 10-year Treasury yield stands at 4.806%, up 2.2 basis points in a 4.760-4.812% range and near a two-decade high, with the 30-year at 5.252% and the 5-year at 4.575%; the latest Federal Reserve H.15 table shows a 4.78% 10-year and a 4.37% 2-year. A 16 September FOMC decision, projections and press conference remain the dominant scheduled macro event, and CPI on 11 September is the next Tier-1 release. VIX near 15.72, up 2.75% in a 15.22-15.94 range, remains low in absolute terms and does not confirm the stress visible in energy and rates, which is itself a cross-asset conflict. The shared cross-asset context file was about 109 minutes old at the cutoff and its futures section was empty, so it was treated as stale and this assessment rests on independent verified research. Confidence is 89 on a live NQ quote timestamped inside the current hour, live ES, VIX and 10-year readings, verified cash-index closes, Federal Reserve H.15 yields, verified crude prices, a verified U.S. calendar and verified geopolitical reporting. The dominant conditional risk over the next 24 hours is a supply headline repricing crude through $100 into thin overnight books, or an oil-driven inflation impulse meeting the U.S. cash open. Neither has produced the shallow-pullback, repeated-extension structure that would justify a higher tail.

lookbackSummary: Across the preceding 24 clock-hours the mapped state stayed EA_ON with tail between 5 and 15 and no reading near the block threshold. The single elevated print was 15 at 14:00 UTC on 8 September during a brief trend-down phase around the U.S. cash open, which reverted within the hour. Stress climbed steadily from 63 to 74 as crude pressed toward $100 on Middle East supply disruption and the 10-year held near a two-decade high, while confidence improved from 83 to 89 as live price-path evidence accumulated. The 09:00 UTC slot on 8 September has no published assessment and is marked unavailable.
outlookSummary: The next 24 hours contain no Tier-1 U.S. macro release; PPI and jobless claims on 10 September at 12:30 UTC fall just outside this window. Conditional tail stays in a 7-13 band and never approaches the block threshold, peaking across the 13:30-15:00 UTC U.S. cash open where an oil-driven inflation impulse meeting the opening auction is the specific failure mode of concern, with a secondary step at 17:00 UTC for the 10-year note auction and the Apple keynote. Stress holds in the high band at 75-77 on the unresolved Middle East energy-supply premium and a 4.806% 10-year. Confidence decays from 89 to 78 with projection distance. The standing conditional amplifier is a fresh escalation headline repricing crude through $100 into thin overnight books; observed structure would have to turn one-way, with shallow pullbacks and repeated extension after failed retracements, before tail moved materially higher.
